children: shares rose 0.70% premarket after BMO Capital reiterated an Outperform rating and $135 price target, pointing to proprietary consumer research it says shows Netflix still dominates U.S. streaming. In a survey of 940 U.S. consumers, BMO found 75% subscribe to Netflix and 37% name it their most preferred platform, twice the share of the nearest competitor. The firm argued the stock trading at 16.1x fiscal 2027 estimated adjusted EBITDA is a 31% discount to its five-year average, with a scaling ad business set to accelerate revenue in the U.S. and Canada.

The survey provides deeper metrics on engagement. BMO found 76% of subscribers said they use Netflix multiple times a week, and among subscribers, 37% have tried its podcasts and 36% its games, with early users reporting high satisfaction. BMO reads that as evidence Netflix's push beyond film and television is landing rather than diluting the core service.

BMO's call follows a Wells Fargo downgrade to Underweight with a $57 target, cutting the stock on softening viewership and a thinner second-half content slate, part of a wider read that 39% of Americans dropped at least one streaming subscription in the past six months. Evercore ISI sits between them at a $110 target.

title: Netflix Gets a $135 Bull Call Days After a $57 Cut
